experiment_description: Central concept: a controlled wideband incoherent optical-noise source is used to emulate the excess-noise signature that a collective eavesdropping attack would add to a continuous-variable quantum key distribution (CV-QKD) receiver, so that a later coherent detector-blinding stage can be tested against a known injected-noise baseline. The experiment uses only the Bob-side receiver of a polarization-diverse local-local-oscillator CV-QKD system. The receiver local oscillator is an Aerodiode 1550 nm DFB Model 5 laser driven by a Wavelength Electronics MPL250 laser driver and stabilized by a Wavelength Electronics PTC2.5K-CH temperature controller; its output passes through an optical isolator and an Agiltron LightBend 1x1 PM optical switch into a polarization-diverse receiver. The signal input passes through an Agiltron LightBend 1x1 optical switch and then a PBS that separates polarization components into two polarization-maintaining 50/50 beam splitters. The LO PBS is oriented with its fast axis shifted by 45 degrees relative to the LO polarization so that both receiver arms are illuminated. The two balanced detector channels are Wieserlabs WL-BPD1GA balanced optical receivers with 1.6 GHz bandwidth and DC cut-off below 300 kHz, digitized by a Texas Instruments ADC12DJ3200EVM at 3.2 GHz. The digital processing applied to each acquired horizontal and vertical polarization trace consists of downconversion around 400 MHz to baseband by multiplication with exp(-i 2 pi 400e6 t), root-raised-cosine filtering with roll-off factor 0.95 at 153.6 MBaud, polarization-drift recovery by combining the two polarization components assuming equal distribution between receiver arms, and variance computation. Thermal, shot, and noisy traces are acquired by controlling the receiver optical switches: both paths closed for Var[thermal], LO path open and signal path closed for Var[shot], and both paths open for Var[noisy]. Shot-noise units are defined as SNU = Var[shot] - Var[thermal]. The inferred noise variance is sigma_tilde_squared = Var[noisy]/SNU, the receiver thermal noise is epsilon_th = Var[thermal]/SNU, and the inferred excess noise is epsilon_tilde = (sigma_tilde_squared - 1 - epsilon_th)/(eta*T), using receiver efficiency eta = 0.90 and assumed channel transmission T = 0.5, corresponding to 15 km of standard single-mode fibre. The noise source consists of a Thorlabs EDFA100S erbium-doped fibre amplifier operated without input signal so that its amplified spontaneous emission supplies the incoherent optical noise; this output is attenuated by a Thorlabs V1550A voltage-controlled variable optical attenuator driven by a UNI-T UDP3305S power supply under PC serial control, and then combined through a WBC-2x2-13/15-10/90 90/10 beam splitter. The 90% splitter output is monitored by an OZ-Optics POM-300 optical power meter, with readings converted to the 10% port power using the known splitting ratio. The calibration/reproducibility measurement consists of four independent optical-power sweeps over the noise-source setting, varying the monitored noise power from -13.6 dBm to -51.25 dBm with smaller steps at higher attenuation. The spatial/geometric scope is the full two-arm polarization-diverse receiver input and both balanced-detector outputs after digital polarization recombination; reproducibility is assessed by comparing all four repeated sweeps over the same optical path and receiver processing chain. The measurement is configured to determine whether the ASE source provides a reproducible mapping from optical noise power to inferred CV-QKD excess noise in SNU.

experiment_description: Central concept: a coherent detector-blinding source is built to force an AC-coupled balanced detector in a real CV-QKD receiver into a nonlinear or clipped response regime. The attack concept uses a detuned optical field to exploit wavelength-dependent imbalance in the receiver optics and uses temporal modulation to pass through the balanced detector AC coupling, rather than relying on a constant optical blinding level. The tested receiver is the same polarization-diverse CV-QKD Bob receiver described in the paper: an Aerodiode 1550 nm DFB local oscillator, PBS splitting into two polarization-maintaining 50/50 beam splitters, two Wieserlabs WL-BPD1GA balanced optical receivers with 1.6 GHz bandwidth and low-frequency cut-off below 300 kHz, and a Texas Instruments ADC12DJ3200EVM digitizer sampling at 3.2 GHz with 12-bit precision. The blinding source consists of a Sumitomo Electric Industries SLV5410 laser diode emitting at 1344 nm. The diode current is supplied by a Rigol DG1032 function generator, enabling direct square-wave optical modulation at 10 MHz, and the diode temperature is controlled with a Thorlabs TED200C temperature controller. The modulated blinding field passes through a Thorlabs V1550A voltage-controlled variable optical attenuator driven by a UNI-T UDP3305S power supply under PC serial control. The attenuated light enters a Thorlabs TD1315R5F1 50/50 dual-window 1310/1550 nm beam splitter; one output is monitored by an OZ Optics POM-600 optical power meter and the other is combined with the signal fibre through a Thorlabs WD1350B wavelength-division multiplexer. A fibre polarization controller after the multiplexer is adjusted while monitoring both balanced-detector outputs so that the blinding-field amplitude delivered to the two polarization receiver arms is matched. For the standalone blinding-response measurement, the horizontal balanced-detector arm is monitored in the time domain while the blinding optical power is swept from -15 dBm to -13 dBm. The measurement scope is the horizontal polarization receiver arm and its ADC output over repeated cycles of the 10 MHz blinding modulation; the two-arm balance of the injected blinding field is checked by comparing the output amplitudes of both balanced receivers during polarization adjustment. The measurement is configured to identify the receiver stage that limits the response and to determine the blinding level at which the horizontal-channel digitized output reaches full-scale clipping.

receiver_limiting_stage_under_blinding.description: The receiver component identified as the stage that limits the digitized response under the modulated 1344 nm blinding field.

blinding_power_for_full_scale_adc_clippi.description: The monitored blinding optical power at which the horizontal receiver output reaches full-scale digitized clipping under the specified square-wave blinding modulation.

full_scale_adc_minimum_count_under_blind.description: The lower digitized ADC count reached by the horizontal receiver output during full-scale clipping under the specified blinding condition.

full_scale_adc_maximum_count_under_blind.description: The upper digitized ADC count reached by the horizontal receiver output during full-scale clipping under the specified blinding condition.

experiment_description: Central concept: the complete coherent detector-blinding attack is tested on a real CV-QKD receiver by combining an ASE noise source, representing the excess-noise impact of a collective attack, with a modulated detuned blinding source that drives the receiver out of its normal linear operating regime. The apparatus is a reduced Bob-only implementation of the attack scenario: the exploitation stage is represented by the calibrated EDFA-based incoherent-noise source and the enabling stage is represented by the 1344 nm modulated blinding source. The receiver is the polarization-diverse local-local-oscillator CV-QKD receiver with Aerodiode 1550 nm DFB LO, Agiltron optical switches for thermal/shot/noisy acquisitions, PBS-based polarization splitting, two polarization-maintaining 50/50 beam splitters, two Wieserlabs WL-BPD1GA balanced optical receivers with 1.6 GHz bandwidth and 300 kHz low-frequency cut-off, and a Texas Instruments ADC12DJ3200EVM digitizer at 3.2 GHz. Digital processing consists of 400 MHz frequency recovery, root-raised-cosine filtering with roll-off 0.95 and 153.6 MBaud symbol rate, two-polarization combination for polarization-drift recovery, and variance computation. Shot-noise units are defined as SNU = Var[shot] - Var[thermal], with epsilon_tilde = (Var[noisy]/SNU - 1 - Var[thermal]/SNU)/(eta*T), eta = 0.90, and assumed channel transmission T = 0.5. The noise source is the Thorlabs EDFA100S ASE source attenuated by a Thorlabs V1550A VOA and injected through the 90/10 splitter path; the fixed corrected noise powers used in the attack measurement are -27.0 dBm, -28.3 dBm, -29.9 dBm, -30.8 dBm, and -31.8 dBm. The blinding source is the Sumitomo Electric Industries SLV5410 1344 nm diode directly square-wave modulated at 10 MHz by a Rigol DG1032, temperature controlled by a Thorlabs TED200C, attenuated by a Thorlabs V1550A VOA, monitored after a Thorlabs TD1315R5F1 50/50 beam splitter with an OZ Optics POM-600 optical power meter, and injected through a Thorlabs WD1350B wavelength-division multiplexer followed by a polarization controller adjusted to balance the blinding amplitudes in the receiver arms. The independent blinding-power sweep spans -15.64536 dBm to -12.53858 dBm for each fixed noise-source setting. The measurement scope is the complete two-balanced-detector polarization-diverse receiver after digital polarization recombination, with five independent fixed injected-noise conditions compared across the same blinding-power sweep. For evaluating whether a blinded receiver would accept a key, the receiver-estimated excess noise is compared with the positive-key-rate excess-noise threshold computed using the Denys-Brown-Leverrier arbitrary-modulation security proof for a probabilistically shaped 64-QAM constellation with Maxwell-Boltzmann-distributed constellation points at T = 0.5. The reported hiding metric is the minimum blinding optical power at which the receiver-estimated excess noise for a given calibrated injected excess noise falls below that positive-key-rate threshold.

positive_key_rate_excess_noise_threshold.description: The excess-noise threshold in shot-noise units used as the comparison level for whether the receiver would report a positive asymptotic key rate under the stated probabilistically shaped 64-QAM security analysis.
